items.name: Review
items.description: Review the current changes for bugs, risky edits and missing tests, most severe first.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: review
command.template:
Review the changes in this project that are not committed yet (`git diff` and `git diff --staged`). If there are none, review the last commit.

For each problem, give the file and line, what goes wrong and for which input, and the smallest fix. Put the most severe first. Check correctness, error handling, security, and tests that would catch a regression.
Do not list style preferences. If you find nothing real, say so.

Focus: $ARGUMENTS

items.name: Handoff
items.description: Write a handoff note so another person or session can pick this work up cold.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: handoff
command.template:
Write a handoff note for the work in this session so someone with no context can continue it.

Include: the goal, what is done (with file paths and commit or PR ids), what is not done, every open question or decision, how to run and check it, and the first next step. List open items in full; do not summarise them away.

Save it as HANDOFF.md in the project root unless I say otherwise. $ARGUMENTS

items.name: Standup
items.description: Summarise what changed in this project since yesterday, for a standup or status update.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: standup
command.template:
Write a short standup update for this project from its git history since yesterday morning (`git log --since=yesterday --stat`).

Three parts: Done (what shipped, one line each), Next (what the open branches and TODOs point to), Blocked (anything waiting on someone). Plain language, no hype.

$ARGUMENTS

items.name: Explain
items.description: Explain a file, function or folder: what it does, how data moves through it, and what depends on it.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: explain
command.template:
Explain $ARGUMENTS to someone new to this codebase.

Start with what it is for in one or two sentences. Then how it works step by step, quoting the real code with file paths and line numbers, what calls it and what it calls, and anything surprising. Say what you did not check.

items.name: Test
items.description: Write tests for a file or change that fail on the bug they guard, using the project's own test setup.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: test
command.template:
Write tests for $ARGUMENTS (if empty: the uncommitted changes).

Use the test framework and folder this project already uses. Test what a caller sees: return values, rendered text, HTTP responses. Mock only the network, the clock and outside services.
Each test must fail if the behaviour it covers breaks. Run the tests and show the result.

items.name: Fix
items.description: Find why the build, tests or a reported error fail, fix the cause, and show it passing.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: fix
command.template:
Something is failing: $ARGUMENTS (if empty: run the tests and the build and take the first failure).

Reproduce it first. Find the cause, not the symptom, and fix it with the smallest change. Run the failing check again and show it passing. Say what you did not check.

items.name: Commit
items.description: Stage the current work and write a commit message that says what changed and why.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: commit
command.template:
Look at `git status` and `git diff`. Group the changes; if they are unrelated, say so and ask before committing them together.

Write a commit message: a short subject in the imperative, then a body that says why. Do not commit secrets, build output or files listed in .gitignore. Show the message before committing. $ARGUMENTS

items.name: Pull request
items.description: Write the pull request title and description for this branch from its commits and diff.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: pr
command.template:
Write a pull request for this branch against its base (`git log` and `git diff` from the merge base).

Title: what it does, under 70 characters. Description: why, what changed (by area), how it was tested, and anything a reviewer should look at first. $ARGUMENTS

items.name: Plan
items.description: Turn a request into a step-by-step plan with the files to change, risks and how to check each step.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: plan
command.template:
Make a plan for: $ARGUMENTS

Read the code it touches first. List the steps in order, each with the files it changes and how to check it worked. Name the risks and open questions. Do not change any code yet.

items.name: Refactor
items.description: Restructure code without changing what it does, with tests run before and after.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: refactor
command.template:
Refactor $ARGUMENTS without changing its behaviour.

Run the tests first and note the result. Make the change in small steps. Run the tests again; they must give the same result. Keep public names unless I ask otherwise.

items.name: Docs
items.description: Update the README and docs to match the code as it is now.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: docs
command.template:
Update the documentation for $ARGUMENTS (if empty: the uncommitted changes).

Find the docs that describe this code (README, docs folder, comments on public functions). Change only what is now wrong or missing. Use plain language and real examples from the code.

items.name: Security review
items.description: Check the current changes for security problems: injection, secrets, auth gaps and unsafe input.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: security
command.template:
Review $ARGUMENTS (if empty: the uncommitted changes) for security problems.

Check: user input that reaches a shell, SQL, HTML or file path; secrets in code or logs; missing auth or permission checks; unsafe defaults. For each finding give the file and line, how it could be used, and the fix. If nothing is real, say so.

items.name: Debug
items.description: Work out why something behaves wrongly, step by step, with evidence before any fix.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: debug
command.template:
Debug this: $ARGUMENTS

Say what should happen and what happens. Form one hypothesis at a time and test it with logs, a small script or the debugger. Show the evidence for the cause before proposing a fix.

items.name: Changelog
items.description: Write release notes from the commits since the last tag, grouped for the people who use it.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: changelog
command.template:
Write release notes from the commits since the last tag (`git describe --tags --abbrev=0`, then `git log`).

Group them as Added, Changed and Fixed. One line each, written for the people who use the product, not for developers. Leave out internal-only changes. $ARGUMENTS

items.name: Onboard
items.description: A tour of this codebase for someone new: what it is, how it runs, and where things live.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: onboard
command.template:
Give me a tour of this codebase. $ARGUMENTS

Cover: what it does, how to run it and its tests, the main folders and what each holds, how a request or action flows through it, and the three files to read first. Quote real paths.

items.name: TODOs
items.description: Collect the TODO, FIXME and HACK notes in the project into one ranked list.
items.author: Allternit

command.name: todo
command.template:
Find every TODO, FIXME and HACK comment in this project (skip node_modules, build output and vendored code).

List them with file and line, grouped by area, most important first, with one line on what each needs. $ARGUMENTS
